headline: Computational primer and read-resolution tools for pathogen sequencing identification
label: Pathogen Sequencing Design Tools
summary: Accessible, validated design and classification tools increasingly determine which pathogen and viral sequences are recovered from complex samples.
synthesis: The common thread is computational design upstream of sequencing-based identification, where primer parameters, enrichment strategy, or read-resolution algorithms determine which target sequences are recovered from complex samples. ColabPCR refines Primer3 parameters and screens candidate primers through BLASTn off-target counts and restriction-site checks in a Google Colaboratory notebook. The MSSPE preprint applies an open-source spiked-primer design algorithm that enriches viral reads from swine slurry and farm wastewater, improving viral detection at shallow sequencing depths. RAMBO operates at a different stage, using UMAP, HDBSCAN and staged consensus to resolve mixed amplicon signals in Nanopore DNA barcoding reads. The Neisseria gonorrhoeae LIN code paper is a lineage nomenclature built on a refined 1430-gene cgMLST and publicly accessible via PubMLST, not a design tool. What is new is emphasis on accessible, validated tooling for these steps rather than on a single organism or platform.
